correctness.rationale: The central construction works, but the frozen Finding asserts without a qualifier that the two exceptional fiber dimensions differ. At the admitted case (k,n)=(2,4) both fibers are P^1; throughout n=2k they have equal dimension and both maps are Goresky–MacPherson small. This also qualifies the 'only for the selected orientation' wording in the Limitations. The proof's explicit dimensions themselves are correct. At S the dual semigroup consists of integer transfers from S to its complement, generated by the e_j-e_i, hence the chart is the rank-one matrix cone, smooth off its origin. Each perturbation has exactly one free coordinate at each vertex, with signed coordinate normals omitting it forming an integral basis of Z^n/Z1. Minimizing a generic functional orders coordinates just as maximizing its negative; the greedy extremizers give the refinement, with no new rays. The incidence charts at a chosen free coordinate yield precisely P^(k-1) or P^(n-k-1) over each fixed point, and there is an isomorphism away from those points. The sole local ray relation requires k=n-k for a canonical support function; then integer values realize it and absence of exceptional divisors gives crepancy. Otherwise X is not Q-Gorenstein, so usual crepancy is unavailable. With r=min(k,n-k), 2(r-1)<n-1; substituting the larger fiber dimension shows that orientation is GM-small exactly in the balanced case. The frozen CHECKER.py and output were inspected, not run: 42 finite rational box-slice checks, 7540 vertices, not proof of the general fan or canonical assertions. Frozen attestation/audit/Lean statuses were not_performed.

evidence: Dolgachev–Hu's theorem for a smooth projective variety at a truly faithful rational cell supplies two natural birational morphisms, isomorphisms off the strictly semistable stratum, with opposite weighted-projective fibers up to the stabilizer component group.

Here the orbit interval in the normalized moment coordinate has integer endpoints from the factors fixed at 0 or 1. Noninteger levels thus have stable free action: a mixed factor forces stabilizer 1. At the wall the strictly semistable closed orbits are exactly the fixed points with k coordinates at 1, each with stabilizer the connected diagonal C*, so the rational cell is truly faithful. Varying the character linearly gives chambers relevant to it in the sense of Definition 3.4.6.
The nearby two Resultary records have different targets and strata: a one-entry-deleted Segre variety, and edge toric varieties of complete multipartite graphs.

evidence: At the weight-k fixed point the k endpoint-1 local coordinates have weight -1, and the other n-k have weight +1. Wall chart invariants are pairwise products, yielding exactly the rank-one determinantal cone. The two chamber quotients of this local representation select a nonzero vector of one sign modulo a free scalar; they are the two usual incidence bundles and have ordinary projective fibers of dimensions k-1 and n-k-1, since all weights have absolute value 1 and there is no component group.

The wall locus is precisely the binomial number of fixed points. The two exceptional loci have codimensions n-k and k respectively, each >=2. Their codimension ensures birational smallness and crepancy whenever the canonical divisor is Q-Cartier. The sole signed ray relation gives Q-Cartier exactly at k=n-k; the two numerical GM comparisons are direct fiber dimension inequalities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two-sided globalization, local models, projectivity and thresholds of the valid core require only substituting the cube representation and its unit weights into the established adjacent-chamber theory and the usual canonical/smallness tests. This is concrete mechanical implication, not the generic observation that toric resolutions exist.

The frozen plus box is (d,lambda)=(1+eps,k). Translating the frozen minus box by eps·1 gives (1+eps,k+n eps). Normalizing d to 1 places the two levels in (k-1,k) and (k,k+1); the wall level is k. originality.rationale: The core construction is already covered as the direct adjacent-chamber case of Dolgachev–Hu's VGIT variation theorem, Theorem 4.2.7 / 0.2.5, for the diagonal scaling torus of (P^1)^n. The box model is exactly the ordinary weight slice of that very quotient in each chamber, not a different globalization. The equal-weight tangent representations identify both local models and exceptional fibers, and canonical and GM-smallness thresholds are direct consequences of those dimensions and the standard toric canonical criterion. This verdict is by implication and identification of the actual maps, not a claim that the source states them verbatim under the name hypersimplex.
residual_risks: No claim is made to have found the earliest explicit hypersimplex wording. The Jojić and Cox–Little–Schenck full-text passages were not accessible in the attempted routes; this is not the basis of the verdict. The direct theorem-level coverage suffices even without a named hypersimplex example.

value.rationale: The example is a useful exposition of elementary VGIT for a product of projective lines. As a research finding, the valid package is exactly the two ordinary adjacent variations, with their standard rank-one fibers and immediate canonical and smallness thresholds, rather than an independent unknown invariant or new globalization. The apparent difference of the fiber dimensions also vanishes on the balanced boundary; correcting that qualifier would leave the covered core and not produce a valuable new claim. No repair is submitted.
